main_text.l: tu contriuisti, sicut in die (quo contriuisti) Midian. Omne quidem prælium, quod fit per præliantem, (fit) cum strepitu& uo-lutatione uestimenti in sanguine: (hoc uero bellum) erit per combustionem & de-uorationem ignis. Quoniam puer natus est nobis, filius datus est nobis, & factus est principatus super humerū eius, uocatumq; est nomen eius, admirabilis, consiliarius, Deus fortis, pater æternitatis, princeps pa-cis. Multiplicatio principatus & pax ipsa (erunt) absq; fine, super solium Dauid& super regnum eius, ut disponat illud & stabi-liat ipsum in iudicio & iustitia, ammodò & usq; in seculum : zelus Domini exercituū faciet hoc. Verbū misit Dominus in Iacob, & cecidit in Israël. Et scient uniuersi popu-li Ephraijm, atq; habitator Samarię, qui dicunt in superbia & magnificentia cordis: Lateres ceciderunt, & politis (lapidibus) ædi-ficabimus: sycomori succisæ sunt, & cedros uendicabimus. Et roborabit Dominus hostes Rezin contra ipsum, & inimicos eius miscebit (contra eum.) Syria erit a priori parte, & Phelistæi a posteriori, deuo-rabunt; Israelem toto ore: nec in omni i-sto auersus est furor eius, sed adhuc manus eius.

page.notes: Handwritten jottings in the right margin ("De Merfia." and "Epitheta.") are manuscript annotations, not printed text, and are left out. The printed text reads "super" and "stabi-liat" etc. where a line-end break occurs; "eius" at the end of the page is the catchword. Long s has been normalised to s throughout. The word "Dauid" carries a small mark after it in the scan, which is not transcribed. The initial fragment "tu" continues from the previous page.
